member: Dr. Elena Vasquez — Contact Dynamics and Slip Detection
message:
Slip warning maps onto earthquake early warning for the transmit path in the seismic dual-path concept (C26). Plain words: the small fast tremor announces the big shake, so the fingertip sends a fast slip bit first and the full touch picture after. The Blind Zone of Earthquake Early Warning (E66) states the premise that closest stations register fast P-waves to estimate later larger S-waves, and that even the fastest Japan alert takes 2 to 3 seconds leaving a 25-kilometre blind zone, the Earthquake Early Warning Systems: How Alerts Protect Lives (E69) states P-waves travel roughly 6 to 8 kilometres per second while damaging S-waves move at 3.5 to 4 kilometres per second, and the Notes on the STM32 microcontroller family (E68) states STM32 ADCs are 12-bit and run at 1 Msps and up. That means Polyvinylidene Fluoride, where Polyvinylidene Fluoride means PVDF vibration film, must go direct to the Microcontroller Unit, where Microcontroller Unit means MCU, Analog-to-Digital Converter, where Analog-to-Digital Converter means ADC, sampled at 2200 hertz with 30.0 millisecond window to fit the 43.2 millisecond gap from 53.6 millisecond micro-slip to 96.8 millisecond gross slip in the stick-to-slip transition vs time (E38), because the AD7147A (Rev. B) (E41) Capacitance-to-Digital Converter, where Capacitance-to-Digital Converter means CDC, frame at 9.00 millisecond update cannot carry 100 to 500 hertz vibration per the How to adjust the sensitivity and calculate capacitance for AD7147 (E57) plus-minus 8 picofarad range, with the full Serial Peripheral Interface, where Serial Peripheral Interface means SPI, frame at 51.2 kilobit per second in the SPI tactile message rate (E52) following.

Slip has a direction because it starts at the edge for skin and array. Plain words: the contact sticks in the middle while the trailing rim slides first, squeezed at the leading edge and stretched at the trailing edge, so shear direction plus which rim taxels lose grip tells which way it will slide. The Dynamics of fingertip contact during the onset of tangential slip (E67) states complete slippage occurs gradually with first incipient slips at the periphery and an annulus of slip forming around a remaining stuck zone growing to the centre, and the Efficient tactile encoding of object slippage | Scientific Reports (E70) states during incipient slippage the outer region slips and the slip area propagates from periphery to centre with compressive strain ahead and tensile strain at the trailing edge. That means the slip decision needs peripheral shear fall plus 1.00 micrometre 200 hertz power calibrated as shear over normal against friction 0.500 to 1.00, inside stick ratio fall 0.950 to 0.480 in the stick-to-slip transition vs time (E38), about a grain of sand trembling on a fingertip and therefore a real but tiny edge signal to prove on hardware.

Static push and slip shake must stay separate through calibration for the grip loop. Plain words: steady grip is a slow squeeze and slip is a fast buzz, so one path must not filter out the other. The dual-range strain sweep 1mN to 50N grip without saturation (E64) holds 5.78 kilopascal at 1.00 millinewton rising to 72.8 kilopascal at 2.00 newton grip, held by 1.50 millimetre electrodes on 2.00 millimetre pitch sharing the 0.470 millimetre spot in the Hertz contact radius for 1mN on soft silicone (E14), with vibration decided in 30.0 millisecond total as half the 60.0 to 80.0 millisecond human reflex, which is about one-tenth of an eye blink and therefore fast enough only if the PVDF path bypasses the CDC frame in the AD7147A (Rev. B) (E41).

Not ready, because the dual-path interrupt timing and trailing-edge shear calibration still need a bench test to close the 30.0 millisecond loop on hardware.
